h: Shabbos Wine Reveals the Good Hidden in Sorrow

p: The mitzvah of eating three meals on Shabbos
for we derive it from the three times "today,"
and from the Rabbis we find
that they instituted also a mitzvah of drinking wine,
as they said in the Gemara (Berachos 42b):
בְּשַׁבָּת אָדָם קוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן
"On Shabbos a person makes his meal around wine";
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (נָשֹׂא, בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה י, א)
and in the Midrash Rabbah (Naso, Bamidbar Rabbah 10:1):
"With what do you give it delight?
זָכוֹר אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת (שְׁמוֹת כ, ח)
for by Torah law mention with the mouth suffices
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ
along the lines of what is said in the holy Zohar on this parsha
(חֵלֶק ג לג, ב; וְדַף רעא, ב)
'and drink of the wine I have mixed'
For חטה, wheat, is in gematria twenty-two,
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
it does not say "of my wine,"
for it is man who brings forth the matter,
that which flows to him from Heaven;
and about this it says "I have mixed."
And the designation of Torah she'b'al peh
is along the lines of what they said
(בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה נָשֹׂא, בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה י, ד)
and to give the wicked their reward in this world";
if he is worthy, it gladdens him;
if he is not worthy, it desolates him."
That is, for one whose whole aim of joy
which brings wailing to the world,
But the essence of joy is
and for the upright of heart, joy.'"
For a tzaddik is what one is called
מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מִלְחֶמֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרַע
who has a war with the yetzer hara,
and he is a mighty one who conquers his inclination;
while the heart is occupied with the war.
Only after uprightness has come about in his heart,
and he merits what they said
גַּם אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִים אִתּוֹ (מִשְׁלֵי טז, ז)
even his enemies He makes to be at peace with him" (Mishlei 16:7)
And this is the idea of consolation from his mourning and sorrow
אֵין וְהָכֵן (בְּרֵאשִׁית מג, טז) אֶלָּא שַׁבָּת
"'And prepare' (Bereishis 43:16) means nothing other than Shabbos,
'And it shall be on the sixth day that they shall prepare'";
"And they drank and became merry with him."
For now there became clear to them
the attribute of the tzaddik in its completeness,
about which they had been perplexed until then.
when he saw that he had been sold as a slave,
שֶׁזֶּה בָּא עַל סִיבַּת פְּגַם הַבְּרִית
which comes as a result of a blemish of the bris,
he was cursed to be a slave,
and that was as punishment for a blemish of the bris;
and even after he became ruler in Egypt,
his heart was still not at rest about this,
only from the king of Egypt.
Only after all his brothers came
and bowed down to him to the ground
from this it became clear to him
as his brothers had suspected him.
that the sin of the sale had been exacted from them,
the attribute of the tzaddik now became clear to them;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה שָׁתוּ עַתָּה יַחַד
and through this they now drank together
מִיַּיִן הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ (תְּהִלִּים קד, טו)
of the wine that gladdens the heart of man (Tehillim 104:15)
and "wine entered, a secret came out"
that all the sorrow there had been until then
through the deeds of free choice,
it became clear that it had been by individual providence,
from His will, may He be blessed,
"If your sins will be like these years
from the six days of Creation,
they will become white as snow."
שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְגִילָּה ז, ב)
about which our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Megillah 7b):
"A person is obligated to become intoxicated on Purim"
בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי כְּטוֹב לֵב הַמֶּלֶךְ בַּיָּיִן (אֶסְתֵּר א, י)
"on the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine" (Esther 1:10),
about which the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Megillah 12b)
And then there was revealed the inner heart
that they are bound to Him, may He be blessed,
הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה הַמְעַכֵּב
is only from the "leaven in the dough" that holds back;
and from this it became clear
that the corruption of their partaking
and this was yet another cause
to carry out the eradication of Amalek with added distinction.
And from this was born the repose
and the joy in the heart,
"And they had rest from their enemies," etc.
And this is in essence the holiness of Shabbos,
which is the repose and the rest
of the close of the sixth day
of the six days of work;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א מח, ב)
as is said in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 48b):
"On the day that Hashem gives you rest
from your sorrow and from your trouble," etc. (Yeshayahu 14:3),
which refers to the day of Shabbos,
of the six days of work
for then, at the entry of Shabbos,
the repose appears in the heart,
וְעַל זֶה בָּא תַּקָּנַת חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה
And for this came the enactment of our Sages, of blessed memory,
in order to be consoled from one's mourning and sorrow
of the six days of work.
"And I will repay consolation to him and to his mourners"
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קכג, א)
over the corruption of the deeds
in the six days of work.
And in the holiness of the day of Shabbos
rest and joy are born in the heart,
for everything has become clear as good.
And this mitzvah is specifically Rabbinic,
from the side of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is called "the wine of the Torah,"
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בִּנְדָרִים כב, ב)
along the lines of what they said (Nedarim 22b):
only the Five Books of the Torah, etc.,
כִּי בְּרוֹב חָכְמָה רוֹב כָּעַס (קֹהֶלֶת א, יח)
for 'in much wisdom is much anger'" (Koheles 1:18).
that came from the side of the yetzer hara
to rectify this and to make clear
וְגַם בְּמִילַת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And also at the bris of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
to be circumcised at eight days,
which is the meal of the bris milah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פִּרְקֵי דְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק כט
as they said (Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer ch. 29,
"He-g mal" — on the eighth day he circumcised.
And also regarding the meal of Lot and the angels
"And he made them a feast (mishteh)," etc.;
"And I will fetch a morsel of bread."
וְהַיְינוּ כִּי אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
That is, because Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
for the yetzer hara has no dominion over them;
which is not so with Lot,
for whom this was the cause of his rescue,
that wine would come his way in the cave,
so that from this would descend
the root of the kingship of the House of David and Mashiach,
the ultimate end of the blemish of Adam HaRishon
as they said in the Midrash Rabbah
"'That we may preserve seed from our father' (Bereishis 19:32)
that seed which comes from elsewhere";
and their intent was for the sake of Heaven
that is stated at the bris of Yitzchak
is because then there was clarified as well
of the sin of Adam HaRishon,
about whom the Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 38b):
That is: by his original making
עַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת בִּבְחִירָתוֹ
through eating from the Tree of Knowledge by his own choice,
a foreskin was drawn over him,
all the descendants that branched out from him
are born with the blemish of the foreskin.
And when there appeared in the world
the mitzvah of milah at eight days, for the first time,
it became clear that there is a rectification in the begetting
וּמַחַץ מַכָּתוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם יִרְפָּא (יְשַׁעְיָה ל, כו)
"And He will heal the wound of the blow of the world" (Yeshayahu 30:26).
